llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for managing Amara through OOMOL, but its first-time setup tells the agent to run unverified remote installer scripts directly in a shell.

dimensions.detail: The declared tool access is limited to Bash(oo *), and credentials are described as injected server-side by OOMOL, but the connector can still read and mutate Amara account data once connected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: If the oo CLI is missing, the setup instructions use curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex commands from cli.oomol.com without checksum, signature, version pinning, or explicit user approval before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language says to use the skill for ANY Amara request, which is broad, but the runtime instructions are Amara-specific and include confirmation requirements for write and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not install persistence itself, but it directs one-time CLI installation and account connection setup that persist outside a single skill run.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities match its stated Amara integration purpose: it uses the OOMOL oo CLI to inspect connector schemas and run Amara read, write, and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the first-time setup path before installing. Prefer installing the oo CLI from a trusted, versioned source with integrity verification, and do not let an agent run the remote installer automatically. After installation, use the skill only with an Amara account you intend OOMOL to access, and carefully confirm any write or destructive Amara action payload before it runs.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The remote installer commands are real artifact text in the first-time setup section; installation guidance is related to using the CLI, but direct shell execution of mutable remote scripts is under-scoped and high-impact compared with safer install instructions.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad ANY Amara request wording is present, but it is consistent with a single-service Amara connector and is mitigated by action tagging plus explicit confirmation requirements for write and destructive actions.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported by the artifact's curl-to-bash and irm-to-iex setup commands; this is a review concern, not evidence of bundled malicious code or intentional deception.
